concepts.title: 1. Translating Verbal Conditions to Quadratics
concepts.subtitle: Define variables, relationships, and constraints
concepts.summary: Choose one unknown, express related quantities in terms of it, and state conditions such as positivity.
concepts.trap: Writing equations before defining the variable.

concepts.title: 2. Forming and Simplifying the Quadratic
concepts.subtitle: Translate → expand → standard form
concepts.summary: Form the contextual relation, expand products or clear denominators, and collect terms into ax²+bx+c=0.
concepts.trap: Sign errors while transposing or clearing denominators.

concepts.title: 3. Solving the Quadratic
concepts.subtitle: Generate algebraic candidate values
concepts.summary: Solve for every algebraic candidate before deciding which values are valid in context.
concepts.trap: Discarding a root before checking what x represents.

concepts.title: 4. Context Validation
concepts.subtitle: Turn candidates into the real answer
concepts.summary: Check positivity, dimensions, speed, time, quantity, and units before stating the final answer.
concepts.trap: Reporting a mathematically valid but physically impossible value.

concepts.title: 5. Verifying the Original Relationship
concepts.subtitle: Audit the final contextual result
concepts.summary: Substitute the accepted values back into the original word relationship to verify the model and arithmetic.
concepts.trap: Checking only the derived quadratic instead of the original contextual relationship.

worked_examples.title: Type 1: Consecutive positive integers
worked_examples.problem: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 306. Find the integers.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} First integer &= x \\ Second integer &= x+1 \end{aligned}

steps.reason: The negative candidate is rejected because positive integers are required.

worked_examples.conclusion: The consecutive positive integers are 17 and 18.

worked_examples.title: Type 2: Right-triangle dimensions
worked_examples.problem: A right triangle has legs differing by 4 cm and hypotenuse 20 cm. Find the legs.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} First leg &= x \\ Second leg &= x+4 \end{aligned}
\begin{aligned} First leg &= 12 cm \\ Second leg &= 16 cm \end{aligned}
steps.reason: Negative length is not physically meaningful.

worked_examples.conclusion: The legs are 12 cm and 16 cm.

worked_examples.title: Type 3: Train speed
worked_examples.problem: A train covers 360 km. Increasing its speed by 5 km/h reduces the journey time by 1 hour. Find the original speed.

steps.statement: Define the original and increased speeds.
steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} Original speed &= x km/h \\ Increased speed &= x+5 km/h \end{aligned}

steps.reason: Time equals distance divided by speed.

steps.statement: Clear denominators and form the quadratic.
steps.reason: Multiplying by x(x+5) and simplifying gives the quadratic.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} Original speed &= 40 km/h \\ Increased speed &= 45 km/h \end{aligned}
steps.reason: A travel speed must be positive.

worked_examples.title: Type 4: Pipes filling a tank
worked_examples.problem: One pipe fills a tank in 4 hours and another takes 2 hours longer. Together they fill the tank in 12/5 hours. Find the individual times.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} First pipe time &= x h \\ Second pipe time &= x+2 h \end{aligned}
steps.reason: The second pipe takes 2 hours longer.

steps.statement: Clear denominators and form the quadratic.
steps.reason: Multiplying by x(x+2) gives the quadratic.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} First pipe &= 4 h \\ Second pipe &= 6 h \end{aligned}

worked_examples.conclusion: The pipes take 4 hours and 6 hours individually.

worked_examples.title: Type 5: Commercial price and quantity
worked_examples.problem: An item costs ₹50 each for 25 items. If the price rises by x rupees and the quantity falls by x items, total expenditure remains unchanged at ₹1100. Find the feasible x.

steps.statement: Define the changed price and quantity.
steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} New price &= 50+x rupees \\ New quantity &= 25-x items \end{aligned}

steps.reason: Expenditure equals price per item multiplied by quantity.

steps.calculation: \begin{aligned} New price &= 55 rupees \\ New quantity &= 20 items \end{aligned}
steps.reason: The positive candidate gives meaningful commercial values.
